concerns.text: Task T014 (Normalization) depends on T013 (Full Data Stream) and T051 (Verification), but T013 is marked `[ ]` (incomplete) while T014 is marked `[X]` (complete). A task consuming a full data stream cannot be complete if the producer (T013) is incomplete. This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' rule.

Task T015 (Co-occurrence Matrix) depends on T013 (Full Data Stream) and T014 (Normalization). T013 is `[ ]` (incomplete) and T014 is `[X]` (complete). The matrix cannot be built without the normalized data stream. The ordering implies T015 can proceed before T013 finishes, which is impossible.

Task T016 (Semantic Similarity) depends on T014c (Embeddings) and T013. T014c is `[X]` (complete) but T013 is `[ ]` (incomplete). While embeddings might be independent, the task description implies a join with the full dataset context. More critically, T016 is marked `[ ]` (incomplete) but depends on T014c which is `[X]`, creating a valid dependency chain, but the overall Phase 2 state is inconsistent with the completion markers.

Task T017 (Functional Role) depends on T015 (Co-occurrence Matrix) and T014. T015 is `[ ]` (incomplete) and T014 is `[X]` (complete). T017 is marked `[ ]` (incomplete). The dependency chain is logically sound (T015 -> T017), but the completion status of T015 being incomplete while T017 is also incomplete is consistent, yet the presence of T014 as complete while its consumer T015 is incomplete suggests a broken flow in the 'Foundational' phase where all prerequisites should ideally be complete before moving to dependent tasks.

Task T019 (Train/Test Split) depends on T008 (Power Analysis) and T018. T008 depends on T013b (Pilot Data). T013b is `[ ]` (incomplete). T008 is `[X]` (complete). This is a direct violation: T008 cannot be complete if its producer T013b is incomplete. The power analysis cannot be computed without the pilot data variance.

Task T022 (Logistic Regression) depends on T018, T023, T019, T040, T040b. T019 depends on T008 (which depends on incomplete T013b). T022 is marked `[X]` (complete). This is a critical ordering violation: a model fitting task cannot be complete if the data split (T019) and power analysis (T008) it depends on are based on incomplete upstream data (T013b).

Task T025 (Hierarchical Bayesian Model) depends on T019 and T050. T019 depends on T008 (incomplete upstream). T025 is marked `[ ]` (incomplete). This is consistent, but the chain of dependencies starting from T013b (incomplete) -> T008 (complete) -> T019 (incomplete) -> T025 (incomplete) shows a broken link at T008/T013b.

This is a violation: metrics cannot be calculated for a Bayesian model (T025) that has not been fitted (incomplete). The task T029 claims to be complete while its producer T025 is not.
